pages.title: Welcome
pages.subtitle: Consistency is a design problem, not a character test

blocks.heading: Why habits fail
paragraphs: Almost nobody fails at habits because they lack willpower on day one. They fail because the habit had no fixed cue, no obvious place in the day, and no record of whether it happened. By week three the memory of the streak is unreliable and the habit quietly stops.

blocks.heading: What this tracker does about it
items: Assesses the habits you already have, good and bad, before adding more
Attaches each new habit to an existing one — stacking, not scheduling
Identifies the cue that starts it and the reward that ends it
Records the streak in ink so the count is not a memory
Analyses the misses, because two misses in a row is where habits die

blocks.heading: Sixty-six days, not twenty-one
paragraphs: Twenty-one days is a myth traceable to a plastic surgeon's observation about patients adjusting to a new face. The measured median for a habit becoming automatic is closer to sixty-six days, with wide variance by difficulty. The builder pages are sized accordingly.

blocks.heading: Start with three
paragraphs: Three habits, tracked properly, beat ten tracked for a fortnight. The assessment page exists to stop you starting with ten.

pages.title: Instructions
pages.subtitle: One evening to set up, thirty seconds a day to run

blocks.heading: Choose your size
paragraphs: Four sizes are included and all four contain identical pages. A4 and US Letter suit the desk. A5 and Half Letter suit a tablet or a bag, and print two-up on a full sheet.

blocks.heading: Set up once
items: Run the Habit Assessment on the habits you already have
Pick one keystone habit and no more than two others
Sort them into categories so you can see where your life is thin
Fill a Cue, Routine, Reward page for each
Attach each to an existing habit on the Stacking page

blocks.heading: Every day
items: Tick the Daily Habit Tracker — thirty seconds, same time
Mark the streak on the Streak Tracker
If you missed one, write why on the Missed Habit Analysis page the same day

blocks.heading: Every week and month
items: Weekly Review — which held, which slipped, and the trigger behind it
Monthly Review — success rate and whether the habit is becoming automatic
One line on the Progress Dashboard

blocks.heading: Digital use
items: Import the PDF as a document, not as an image
Switch to read mode to tap links, write mode to write
Use the Daily tab to reach today's tracker from any page

pages.title: Habit Building Guide
pages.subtitle: Six rules, and why each one holds

blocks.heading: Make it obvious, or it will not happen
paragraphs: A habit with no fixed cue depends on remembering, and remembering depends on a good day. Attach it to something that already happens without fail — the kettle boiling, the laptop closing, the alarm going off.

blocks.heading: Stack, do not schedule
paragraphs: "After I pour my coffee, I write three lines" survives a chaotic week. "At 07:30 I write" does not survive a single early meeting.

blocks.heading: Shrink it until it is embarrassing
items: Two minutes is a starting size, not a failure
The goal for the first fortnight is attendance, not performance
Scale up only after fourteen unbroken days
A habit you can do tired is a habit you keep

blocks.heading: Never miss twice
paragraphs: One missed day is noise. Two missed days is the new pattern forming. The Missed Habit Analysis page exists for the day after, and it is the highest-value page in this tracker.

blocks.heading: Keystone habits pull others behind them
paragraphs: Sleep, movement and a planned morning tend to drag several other habits with them at no extra cost. Start with one of those rather than with the habit you feel guiltiest about.

blocks.heading: Track the rate, not the feeling
paragraphs: A habit held nineteen days out of thirty feels like failure and is a sixty-three per cent success rate against a baseline of zero. The Success Rate pages exist to correct that distortion.
